PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    my @x; eval { @{1, local $x[0][0]} = 1; }; print "A: [", ($@ || 'NO-DIE'), "]";
  perl: Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference at ... line 2.
  PCL : Undefined subroutine &main::local called at (eval 0) line 0.

EMITTED CL (./pl2cl on that file):
    (p-cast-@ (progn 1 (p-scalar-ctx (pl-local (p-aref-argbox (p-aref-argbox @x 0) 0)))))
-- `local` reached the generic funcall arm.  The LEADING spellings work:
`local $x[0][0]` as a statement, `\(local $y)` and `(1, local $y)` in a list all
lower correctly (probe p8-local-expr.pl), so it is specifically `local` that is
not the first term of the expression it sits in.

NB the VALUE half of multideref.t 46/48 is a ruled accepted divergence
(docs/not-supported.md '`local` on hash/array elements and typeglobs', the
RT #130727 quirk): PCL localizes+vivifies where perl dies.  This task is only
the emission bug -- a `local` PCL cannot lower must not become a call to a
function that does not exist.
subject: BUG (rule 12, loud): `local` in a NON-LEADING expression position lowers to a call to a nonexistent `pl-local` -- `@{1, local $x[0][0]} = 1` and `0for%{scalar local$0[0]}` die "Undefined subroutine &main::local"
